THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:23.2.2012 PASSED IN MVC NO.1463/2008 ON THE FILE OF THE PRESIDING OFFICER,
FAST TRACK COURT, KUNDAPURA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. The undisputed facts are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 20.10.2008 at about 7.30 a.m., near Thomabattu Shalegudde, Hengavalli Village,
Kundapura Taluk when the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-20-B-1929, in which the claimant was travelling was capsized due to rash and negligent driving of the driver.

Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.
3.
Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.

4. The Tribunal has granted the compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl.No.
Particulars

Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Pain and Agony 25,000.00 2.

Medical expenses, 30,000.00 conveyance, special diet, nourishment and attendant charges 3. Loss of income during 9,000.00 treatment period 4. Future loss of income or 38,800.00 future loss of earning capacity
5. Loss of amenities in life 5,000.00

sentences.text: 6. Future medical expenses Nil Total 1,07,800.00 5.

In the present case, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant has sustained fracture of right femur and injuries sustained on her right leg and right knee which is grievous in nature.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, the compensation awarded under the head 'Pain and Agony is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.

6. Further, the compensation granted under the head 'medical expenses including conveyance,
special diet, nourishment and attendant charges' is on the lesser side.
Evidence on record proves that the claimant had made expenditure of Rs.25,357/- towards medical expenses and hospital charges.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.25,357/- is awarded under the head 'medical expenses'.

Further, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head incidental expenses like food, nourishment,
conveyance, attendant charges, etc.
7.
The Tribunal has assessed that the claimant had suffered functional disability of 6%.

Therefore,
the same is kept in tact.
The accident was occurred in the year 2008.
Therefore, the notional income would be Rs.4,500/-.
As the claimant was aged 20 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.

Hence, the 'loss of future income due to disability' is hereby re-assessed and quantified as under:
Rs.4,500 x 6/100 x 18 x 12 = Rs.58,320/-

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.58,320/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future income due to disability'.
8.
Further, a sum of Rs.22,500/-(RS. 4,500 x 5 months) is awarded under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.

9. The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities'
which is on the lesser side.
Therefore, the same is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.
10. The Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head 'future medical expenses'.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded.

11. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:

Particulars

Compensation No. awarded (in Rs.)
1.
Pain and Agony 40,000.00 2.
Medical expenses 25,357.00 3.
Incidental expenses like food, 25,000.00 nourishment, conveyance, attendant charges, etc.

sentences.text: Loss of income during treatment 20,000.00 period 4.
Future loss of income or future loss 58,320.00 of earning capacity 5. Loss of amenities in life 35,000.00 6.
Future medical expenses 25,000.00 TOTAL 2,28,677.00 12.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.1,07,880/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.2,28,677/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,20,877/- (Rs.2,28,677 - Rs.1,07,800) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1463/2008 is hereby modified holding the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,20,877/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iii. 
The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 46 days in filing the appeal.
iv. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records along with certified copy of this order without delay.
v. Costs made easy.

vi. Draw award accordingly.
